science_vegetable: Real-time Lorenz strange-attractor bifurcation targeting that fires millisecond pre-strike ionization pulses to lock chaotic lightning onto collector rods at 98% efficiency.
narrative_prose:
"Jane, your differential equation says the upper capacitor bank will arc in ninety seconds, which is fantastic news because I only need forty-five to clip the shunt cable—hold my cider and watch the dielectric gauge!" Hector yelled, his voice cutting through the ozone-laced gale. He was clinging to the Stormbreaker spire, a jagged copper needle thrusting into the heart of a bruised, violet sky. The wind wasn't just blowing; it was screaming, a physical force trying to tear him from the metal. Below him, the Enclave was a cluster of warm, bioluminescent dots in the crater valley, but up here, it was all electricity and adrenaline. 

"The Lorenz attractor model is showing extreme bifurcation," Jane's voice buzzed in his earpiece, dry and irritatingly calm. "We're looking at a deterministic chaos event. If we don't fire the millisecond pre-strike ionization pulses now, the chaotic lightning will scatter. I'm locking the targeting sequence to hit the collector rods at 98% efficiency, but you need to clear the induction zone, Hector."

He laughed, a sharp bark swallowed by the thunder. "I'm clearing it! Just give me ten seconds to secure the primary coupling!" He reached for the heavy, insulated cable, his gloved hands thick and clumsy. Harnessing gigajoules of planetary lightning was the easy part. The physics were clean, mathematical, beautiful. The hard part was this: a half-degree asymmetrical cable coupling that refused to seat properly. He twisted the wrench, leaning his entire body weight into it, his feet slipping on the slick, rain-lashed metal.

"Hector, the potential gradient is spiking," Jane warned. "The step-leader is forming. Get down."

He froze. The thrill of the storm vanished, replaced by a sudden, cold grip in his chest. His obsessive perfectionism flared to life. He stared at the coupling. It wasn't perfect. It was off by a fraction of a millimeter. "The coupling," he muttered, his voice dropping, the adrenaline draining away. "Jane, the coupling is asymmetrical. It's going to cause a harmonic wobble in the field."

"Hector!" Jane shouted, her voice finally losing its measured tone. "I'm firing the laser in three seconds!"

He couldn't move. He couldn't leave it imperfect. The sky above him tore open, a blinding, actinic flash of violet light as Jane's femtosecond laser punched a hole through the atmosphere, creating a plasma channel for the lightning. Far below in the bunker, he knew Jane was watching emerald phase-space butterfly wings rotate across brass-framed CRT monitors, but up here, there was only the terrible perfection of the strike.

Before the sky could connect, a hand grabbed his harness and hauled him backward with brutal force. He tumbled down the slanted roof, slamming into the safety railing next to Kaio, who was breathing hard, his scout gear dripping. "You looked stuck, Stormbreaker," Kaio shouted over the roar of the incoming strike, his voice tight. "I needed to borrow your wrench anyway."
summary: Hector attempts to secure a cable coupling before a lightning strike, but freezes due to an obsessive compulsion, requiring Kaio to rescue him.

sensory_palette.sight_and_color: A violet laser needle stitching the bruised purple thunderhead to a screaming copper spire fifty meters above the valley.
sensory_palette.sound: The roar of the ozone gale and the sharp crack of an incoming megavolt arc.

interactive_features.description: Secure the primary coupling before the 50 kV/m step-leader discharge.
Maintain footing on the slick, rain-lashed metal of the spire.
Force the stubborn 0.5-degree asymmetrical coupling to seat properly.
